articles.title: SJAA Ephemeris
articles.summary: This SJAA Ephemeris outlines the San Jose Astronomical Association's activity calendar for late July, August, and September, including star parties, dark sky weekends, general meetings, and astronomy classes. The article also announces a new default for Ephemeris delivery, shifting to online notification to reduce printing costs, and the termination of the Observatory Fund, with plans to re-direct its contributions to other club initiatives.

articles.title: August 2009
articles.summary: This document presents the NASA Space Place calendar for August 2009, targeting children with daily activities, educational games, and space-related facts. It highlights astronomical events such as the Perseids meteor shower and moon phases, alongside historical anniversaries and creative challenges tied to space and science topics.

articles.title: Penning Penumbral Predictions
articles.summary: This article offers an August 2009 observing guide, detailing the visibility of Jupiter, Neptune, Uranus, Saturn, Venus, Mars, and Pluto. It then focuses on an upcoming penumbral lunar eclipse, analyzing its occurrence as the second in consecutive months and using historical data to demonstrate that such events are not as rare as they initially appear. The piece briefly mentions NASA's LCROSS mission and includes directions to Houge Park for local readers.

articles.title: The Cool Chemistry of Alien Life
articles.summary: NASA's Spitzer Space Telescope has revealed intriguing insights into the potential chemistry of alien life around M-dwarf stars. While acetylene was detected in planet-forming discs, the absence of hydrogen cyanide (HCN), a crucial building block for DNA's adenine, suggests that prebiotic chemistry may unfold differently on planets orbiting these cool stars. This difference is attributed to M-dwarfs' lower ultraviolet light emissions, which are insufficient to break nitrogen bonds required for HCN formation, implying a unique foundation for life beyond Earth.

articles.title: Book Review: Confessions of an Alien Hunter by Seth Shostak
articles.summary: This article is a glowing review of Seth Shostak's book, "Confessions of an Alien Hunter," which offers a concise summary of the first 50 years of the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence (SETI). The book is praised for its humorous and scientific approach to ETI, addressing both extreme viewpoints (ETI believers vs. radical skeptics) and debunking common myths while providing insights into SETI's challenges, history, and the future. The reviewer highly recommends the book for its blend of anecdotes, science, and direct responses to naysayers.

articles.title: The Last Month In Astronomy
articles.summary: This article provides a roundup of astronomy news from June and July 2009, highlighting several significant discoveries and events. Key updates include new insights into exoplanet life, observations of Betelgeuse's shrinking diameter, the launch of the LRO/LCROSS mission, and findings of potential salt on Enceladus. Other topics cover evidence for the Tunguska event, detailed images of nebulae like NGC 7293 and the Swan Nebula, and a re-evaluation of Galileo's potential early discovery of Neptune.

articles.title: It Must Be Astronomical...
articles.summary: This article, titled "It Must Be Astronomical...", highlights the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) telescope loaner program and provides recommendations for observing deep sky objects like M17 and NGC 6440. It also lists upcoming astronomy conferences, promotes a NASA podcast on the Milky Way for the International Year of Astronomy, and includes organizational details for the SJAA, its staff, and contact information.
